thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#98765 - region=az3 severity=high - detected spike in connection resets to inference-shard cluster (shard-7). Auto-page to on-call

pagerduty-bot: PD#98765 assigned to @bob-oncall (SRE) — escalation policy: region-network

bob-oncall: acked. I'm on it, starting triage. any consoles/graphs?

alice-sre: looking at NOC dashboards — syn/fin resets up ~12x since 02:04 UTC, p50 latency up 80ms -> 140ms, error ratio 5.8% 502/504 on model proxy. sending graphs link: https://grafana.redwood/az3/conn-resets

dave-eng: logs from proxy-gateway show repeated `connection reset by peer` to kernel module handling dpdk NICs. grabbing `dmesg` and `ip -s link` now

carla-pm: heads-up — support queue shows multiple customers reporting inference timeouts and degraded throughput; we should estimate impact and notify customers if it spreads

bob-oncall: good. quick mitigation plan: 1) toggle regional soft-fallback to az1/az2 for non-pin customers, 2) drain new streams off shard-7, 3) swap NIC if hardware flagged. executing step 1 now

incident-bot: soft-fallback policy `region-reshuffle-v2` activated by bob-oncall at 02:07 UTC — routing started shifting 35% of new sessions away from az3 to az1/az2; expected ramp 3 mins

alice-sre: confirming route weights changing. current traffic to az3 down to 58% of baseline. tail error-rate for az3 still high, but overall platform error-rate dropping from 5.8% -> 2.1%

dave-eng: posted diagnostics:
```
# sample kernel/log excerpt (sanitized)
[02:05:18] net_eth0: tx timeout, resetting
[02:05:18] eth0: NIC reported link up/down flapping
[02:05:22] dpdk: 0x1 reset on queue 3
[02:06:11] connection reset by peer (shard7-proxy)
```

eve-support: customer impact snapshot: 23 support tickets in last 30m, 6 flagged P1s (timeouts for inference), affected customers mostly on default routing (not pinned) — churn risk high if not resolved quickly

bob-oncall: starting ephemeral warm-pool spinup in az1 for heavy models to absorb redirected load. ask dave to schedule NIC swap with infra if hardware will need replacement

dave-eng: opening infra runbook step: `az3-nic-sanity-check` - running `sudo ethtool -S eth0` and checking driver versions. If flapping continues we'll coordinate rack tech to reseat NIC. I can do soft reset now, performing `sudo ip link set eth0 down && sudo ip link set eth0 up`

carla-pm: draft incident notice for customers: short note saying "redundancy running, routing reshuffle in progress, some customers may see transient errors; engineers are on it" — ok to send once we have stabilization window (t+15m)

alice-sre: stabilization metrics at 02:12 UTC: platform error-rate 1.4%, az3 errors down to 3.2%, latency trending back toward baseline. fallback ramp complete ~02:11. keep monitoring for 10m

bob-oncall: ack. will keep fallback active until hardware check complete. if NIC swap needed, we'll schedule brief maintenance with expected 2–5m packet interruption; will update timeline

dave-eng: performed soft reset at 02:13 UTC — link hasn't flapped in the last 90s. `ethtool` counters show decreases in tx_errors. leaving monitoring hooks for 10m

incident-bot: PD#98765 status changed: acknowledged -> monitoring (by bob-oncall)

eve-support: sending interim message to impacted customers now (cc: carla-pm). template: "We've rerouted traffic to reduce impact; our engineers are investigating an AZ network hardware disruption and will update in 15 minutes."

bob-oncall: handoff plan: I'll keep monitoring for 30 minutes, then hand to on-call night-shift if stable. tagging @alice-sre for secondary watch. If resets return, revert fallback and escalate to full failover

alice-sre: noted. creating a short incident-run log entry and capturing graphs for the postmortem.

carla-pm: thanks team — please capture exact timestamps for fallback activation and NIC reset for incident timeline. will prepare customer postmortem draft after final state

incident-bot: PD#98765 closed (resolved) by bob-oncall at 02:20 UTC — condition: stabilization observed, fallback still active until manual deactivation

bob-oncall: closing notes: root cause suspected intermittent NIC firmware issue causing TX queue resets on shard-7 host group. next steps: schedule replacement BIOS/firmware push to affected hosts in az3, add NIC-level alert thresholds to catch flapping earlier, and run a controlled hardware reseat next maintenance window. filing follow-up ticket INF-4523

alice-sre: thanks — good mitigation. moving to postmortem draft now. :white_check_mark:
